speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are a 34-year-old male with a history of AIDS presenting with decreased vision and seeing black spots in your right eye. To begin my assessment, have you noticed any floaters, flashes of light, or a curtain-like shadow in that eye recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details; your history of AIDS, Kaposi's sarcoma, and recent fungal esophagitis is concerning for an opportunistic infection. Given the sudden onset of floaters and vision loss without pain, have you noticed any new flashes of light or a shadow obscuring part of your visual field?

REQUEST TEST: Fluorescein_Angiography; Ocular_Coagulation_Profile (Vitreous_Hemorrhage, Retinal_Detachment, CMV_Retinitis, Toxoplasmosis).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Fluorescein_Angiography: Granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages; Ocular_Coagulation_Profile: CMV_Retinitis (Confirmed by fundoscopy findings), Vitreous_Hemorrhage (Not detected), Retinal_Detachment (Not detected), Toxoplasmosis (Not detected).

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Decreased vision and black spots in the right eye. I also have No pain, Left eye is asymptomatic.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: AIDS, fungal esophagitis treated with fluconazole, Kaposi's sarcoma Social history: No additional information provided

speaker: Patient
text: No additional symptoms mentioned. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: CMV Retinitis

I have reviewed your test results and the patient's specific history of AIDS with prior Kaposi's sarcoma and fungal esophagitis; the combination of sudden vision loss, black spots, and lack of pain in an immunocompromised patient is classic for Cytomegalovirus retinitis. The mention of Tuberculosis by a previous provider appears to be an error given the acute ocular presentation, so please confirm if you see any "candle wax drippings" or hemorrhages in your affected eye.
